settings.text:
[Read the provisioning docs →](https://docs.sendlit.app/developers/provisioning)

Sends through your provider, not ours

## One organization for you. One team for each customer.

Your backend holds an organization key. For each customer it creates a SendLit team with its own contacts, templates, sequences, suppressions and API key. Mail goes out through the provider you connect, either one shared mailbox for everyone or the customer's own.

## Provision a customer in one API call

Call `POST /provisioning/teams` with your own tenant ID when a customer signs up. You get back a team and its API key. Retries are safe: the same `externalId` returns the same team and never creates a duplicate.

- **Idempotent by your ID.** Calls are keyed on `(organization, externalId)`. A replay returns `created: false`. A replay with different input returns `409 provisioning_conflict`, so a retry can't silently change a tenant.

- **Scoped keys.** The organization key carries only the scopes you grant (`teams:provision`, `teams:read`, `teams:manage`, `teams:keys`, `usage:read`). Each team key reaches exactly one team.

- **Full lifecycle.** Read, update (name, sender, mailing address, quotas), rotate the team key, suspend, resume and archive.

- **Clean offboarding.** When a customer leaves, or a person asks to be removed, delete one contact or every contact in that customer's team over the API or MCP, then archive the team. Opt-outs stay suppressed, so nobody is mailed again.

- **Quotas per customer.** Set daily and monthly send limits for each team on your shared mailbox, and read usage over the API.

- **Audited.** Provisioning actions are written to your organization's audit log. Org owners can "Enter team" to help a customer, and that is recorded too.

[Read the provisioning docs →](https://docs.sendlit.app/developers/provisioning)

[Headless setup guide →](https://docs.sendlit.app/developers/headless-provisioning)

settings.title: Put a real email editor inside your product
settings.description: Two MIT-licensed React packages give you the editor and the building blocks for broadcasts, sequences, contacts and templates. They are controlled components: your app owns the state and the API calls, and they inherit your Tailwind theme.

items.title: EmailEditor
items.description: WYSIWYG block editor. Text, image, link and separator blocks. Register your own blocks. Plug in your own image uploader.

items.title: TemplateChooser
items.description: System and saved templates with real rendered previews, so customers start from something good.

items.title: SequenceEmailList
items.description: The steps of a sequence: select, reorder, delete with confirmation, add from a template.

items.title: TriggerPicker
items.description: Choose what enrols a contact: subscribed, tag added, tag removed.

items.title: ContactFilterBuilder
items.description: Segment builder with tag, email, subscription and signup-date conditions, plus saved segments.

items.title: TagEditor
items.description: Add and remove a contact's tags, with a picker of existing tags.

items.title: SubscriberList
items.description: Paginated subscribers of a broadcast or sequence, with optional profile links.

items.title: SequenceAnalytics
items.description: Sent, open rate, click rate and more for a broadcast or sequence.

items.title: EmailPreview
items.description: A scaled-down preview rendered through the same pipeline as outgoing mail.

settings.text:
- **Your theme.** The components use your shadcn/Tailwind CSS variables (`--primary`, `--background`, `--radius`...), so they match your brand without overrides.

- **Your words.** Every visible string is an optional prop with an English default. You can localise or reword anything without forking.

- **Your blocks.** `EmailEditor` takes a `blocks` array and a `renderContext`, so you can add product-specific blocks such as "course card" or "event". `renderEmailToHtml` turns the document into email-safe HTML.

- **Your layout.** These are building blocks, not fixed pages. Arrange them however your app needs.

settings.caption: React. Requires React 19 and Tailwind. Components are pre-1.0 (0.2.x), so pin versions. Keep SendLit keys on your server and call the API through your backend.

media.alt: Editor UI follows your theme; the email keeps its own colours.

items.description: Each provisioning call sets useOrganizationDefault, teamEspEnabled and teamCanChangeDefault. A send never silently switches provider.

items.title: Bounces and complaints
items.description: Feedback adapters for Amazon SES (SNS), Resend, Postmark, SendGrid and Mailgun feed automatic suppression.

items.title: One-click unsubscribe
items.description: Marketing mail carries List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post (RFC 8058), as Gmail and Yahoo require.

items.title: Domain checks
items.description: SPF, DKIM and DMARC lookups for each provider's From domain, with the exact records to add, which you can surface in your own "verify your domain" screen.

items.title: Your links, your domain

items.title: Warm-up and safeguards
items.description: A new provider ramps up gradually and sends to the most engaged contacts first.

settings.text: SendLit doesn't operate mail servers or IPs. Delivery, dedicated IPs and the per-email cost are between you and your provider.

## Your brand on every screen and every email

- No "Sent with SendLit" footer on Business (it is also off on Pro and self-hosted).

- Provisioned teams have no SendLit login. Your customers use your app, with our components inside it.

- Sender name and Reply-To per customer. From addresses come from the provider you connect.

- Per-team tracking domain, so links in emails use the customer's or your domain.

- Components follow your theme tokens and copy.

Hosted signup forms, the unsubscribe confirmation page and the web archive are served by SendLit. With a tracking domain, their links use your domain.

## What you'd build yourself

Sending an email is the easy part. A customer-facing email product needs all of this, and every piece has edge cases.

settings.text:
## What's not here yet

- **Outbound webhooks** for delivered, bounced and unsubscribed events (tracked in issue #52). For now, poll `GET /delivery-events` and `GET /suppressions`.

- **Custom-event triggers** for sequences (issue #136). Today sequences start on subscribe, tag added or tag removed.

- **Browser tokens.** Call SendLit from your backend and keep keys server-side.

- **Inviting your customers' staff into SendLit.** Provisioned teams are API-only by design.

- **Subscriber preference center** (issue #54).

[See the roadmap on GitHub →](https://github.com/codelitdev/sendlit/issues)

items.question: Does SendLit send the emails?
items.answer: No. Every hosted plan sends through a provider you connect: Amazon SES, any SMTP server, Postmark, Resend, SendGrid or Mailgun. You pay them directly, and the sending reputation stays yours.

items.question: Do my customers need their own email provider?
items.answer: No. Connect one shared organization mailbox and every team can use it, with per-team limits. You can also let some customers connect their own provider (teamEspEnabled).

items.question: How is one customer's data kept apart from another's?
items.answer: Each customer is a separate team with its own contacts, templates, sequences, suppressions and API key. A team key can only reach its own team. Organization keys can't read team data through the provisioning API.

items.question: What happens if one customer sends spam?
items.answer: Suspend that team with one call and everyone else keeps sending. Bounces and complaints are suppressed automatically, and per-team quotas cap how much any one customer can send through your shared mailbox.

items.question: Can I style the components to match my product?
items.answer: Yes. They use your Tailwind/shadcn theme variables, every label is a prop, and you can add your own editor blocks.

items.question: Which React versions are supported?
items.answer: React 19 (^19.2.0) with Tailwind v3 or v4. The packages are at 0.2.x, so pin your versions.

items.question: Can I call SendLit from the browser?
items.answer: Not directly. Keep the organization and team keys on your server and proxy the calls your components need.

items.question: How many customers can I have?
items.answer: Business includes 15 teams. For more, talk to us about Enterprise, or self-host with no team limit.

items.question: What does it cost?
items.answer: Business is $99 a month or $990 a year for 600,000 emails across all teams, plus your provider's own charges.

items.question: Can I see what's happening in a customer's team?
items.answer: Organization owners and admins can see transactional mail activity per team and can choose to enter a team to help. Every entry is recorded in the audit log.

items.question: Can I leave?
items.answer: Yes. The core is open source (AGPL-3.0) and runs with one docker compose up, and the components are MIT.

items.question: Can my customers use AI assistants with it?
items.answer: Yes. The MCP server is team-scoped, so each customer's assistant only reaches that customer's team.
